aiOverview.content: During the March 2026 DHS government shutdown, roughly 60,000 TSA employees were required to work without pay, leading to hundreds quitting and thousands of daily call-outs. As of March 27, 2026, President Trump signed an order to pay TSA employees using alternative funds to alleviate severe staffing shortages and long airport security lines. Impact on TSA and Travel (March 2026): Staffing Shortages: Nearly 500 transportation security officers quit and call-out rates reached 11% nationwide. Security Delays: Long wait times exceeding three hours occurred at some airports. Wait and Pay: Workers missed three paychecks before the order to pay them was signed. Personnel Strain: The Acting TSA Administrator reported that workers faced financial ruin, including selling plasma and sleeping in cars to stay on the job. Operational Changes: Funding Order: Trump's order redirects funds with a "reasonable and logical nexus" to TSA operations to pay employees. ICE Deployment: ICE agents were deployed to airports to assist with staffing shortages. Long-term Threat: The staffing crisis threatens to disrupt the upcoming FIFA World Cup traffic in June. Note: While TSA employees are slated to be paid under the executive order, other DHS employees, including the Coast Guard, may still be unpaid.
